msgs: 17 laps, 30 passes on track and no safety car

a: Mercedes, from P2 on the grid

asks.q: was it actually good or are you being nice
a: 30 passes on track, not counting the ones in the pit lane

asks.q: i know nothing about f1, start there
a: ok so 22 cars, lined up roughly in qualifying order, less any grid penalties
there's no compulsory stop in a sprint, so plenty of cars go the distance on one set

msgs: 22 places changed hands before they even finished lap 1

asks.q: why is the start always so mad
a: cold tyres, cold brakes, full fuel tank and everybody going for the same gap
it's the only moment of the sprint where the whole field is that close

asks.q: does the start decide the sprint
a: track position is everything on most circuits, you lose places on lap 1 and you can spend a long time stuck behind someone slower

msgs: lap 2 was the busiest of the whole sprint

a: yeah, only moves made on track count here
swaps in the pit lane and stuff behind the safety car are left out

msgs: fastest lap of the sprint went to Antonelli

a: no points for it in a sprint, never has been

asks.q: why is it late in the sprint
a: car's light, almost no fuel left, and the track has rubber all over it by then

msgs: P1 Antonelli · P2 Hamilton · P3 Norris

asks.q: was the winner just in the fastest car
a: partly, always. the median lap times are the honest read on who had the pace
the true pace card is the one i'd trust
